To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of the proteinacious inhibitor PliI in complex with its lysozyme target is the first to provide a structural explanation for the inhibitory mechanism in this class of lysozyme inhibitors at the atomic level and that it is the first structure of a lysozyme in complex with a proteinacious inhibitor.

the structure of the protein inhibitor PliI-Aeromonas hydrophlia in complex with its bacterial lysozyme substrate reveals a novel `key-lock' mechanism that explains the inhibitory activity at the atomic level, and that this mechanism is similar to that found in all other lysozyme inhibitors.
the structure of the i-type lyoszyme inhibitor from A. hydrophila in a complex with its target i-type lysoyzme from Meretrix meretrix is reported.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure-function analysis of the proteinaceous inhibitors of lysozyme produced by bacteria.
the development of a novel class of antibacterial compounds, based on the inhibition of lysozymes, which are important virulence factors in Gram-negative bacteria.
the development of new antibiotics, which is a major goal of the European Union and of other countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the PliA-Ah/ML-LyzC complex is the first structure of the PII family of lysozyme inhibitors in complex with its cognate substrate.
the structure of the PliA-hydrophila in complex to the lysozymes of Meretrix lusciora is the first to describe the mechanism of the Pii inhibitor family at the atomic resolution.
lysozyme inhibition by proteinaceous inhibitors is a very efficient mechanism of bacterial defence against host lysozyme activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of PliI in complex with its lysozyme target is reported, which is the first structure of a proteinaceous inhibitor from the PliI class of inhibitors and the first to explain its mechanism of action at the atomic level.

we have determined the structure of PliI in complex with its cognate target lysozymes, which is a first example of the i-type lytic enzyme inhibitors, and the structural data are used to rationalize the inhibitory mechanism.

we are able to explain the inhibiting mechanism of PliI family inhibitors at the atomic level, and the accumulated structural data indicate that in all the cases an extensive interface, either of a single or of a double `keylock' type, is formed, resulting highly efficient inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of a proteinaceous inhibitor in complex with its substrate provides a unique opportunity for understanding the inhibitory mechanism at the molecular level.
a single point mutant of PliI, which has lost the ability to inhibit the lysozymes from Meretrix and Nereis, can efficiently inhibit the lysoyzmes from other sources.
the PliI inhibitor from Aeromonus hydrophila forms a key-lock interface with its target lyo­zyme.
